title: Future with Going To
tagline: plans and evidence: be going to + base verb
why: We use going to for plans we have already made and for things we can see coming. It is one of the most common ways to talk about the future in English.
know: the form am / is / are going to + base verb
phrases that often go with it: Look!, Be careful!, I've decided, one day
understand: the difference between a plan made before you speak (going to) and a decision made now (will)
why we use going to when we can see that something is about to happen
able: talk about your plans for the weekend, the year or your life
make predictions from what you can see now
ask What are you going to do? correctly
mistakes: I going to visit my parents on the weekend.
I am going to visit my parents on the weekend.
She's going to looks for a new apartment.
She's going to look for a new apartment.
Look at those clouds! It will rain.
Look at those clouds! It's going to rain.
Do you going to take the course?
Are you going to take the course?
I've bought running shoes because I will start jogging.
I've bought running shoes because I'm going to start jogging.
use: Plans and intentions you decided before speaking: I'm going to look for a new job this year.
Predictions from evidence you can see now: Look at that sky! It's going to rain.
Going to or will? A: We need eggs. B: I know. I'm going to buy some later. (already planned) / B: Oh! I'll buy some. (decided now)
form: I am going to / he, she, it is going to / you, we, they are going to + base verb
I'm not going to stay. She isn't going to come. They aren't going to wait.
Are you going to call him? What is she going to do?
signals: tonight, this weekend, next month, one day, I've decided, I've already...; evidence words: Look!, Watch out!, Be careful!, Hurry up!
tip: Ask yourself: did I decide before speaking? Use going to. Am I deciding now? Use will. Can I see it coming? Use going to.

pick.q: Look at those dark clouds! It ___ rain.
pick.why: You can see the evidence now (dark clouds), so use going to: It's going to rain.

pick.q: I've saved enough money. I ___ buy a new laptop next month.
pick.why: This plan was made before speaking (the money is saved), so use going to.

pick.q: She ___ going to start a new job on Monday.
pick.why: With she, use is: She is going to start.

pick.q: I hear you bought a bike. Are you going to ___ your car now?
pick.why: After going to, always use the base verb: going to sell.

pick.q: A: Why are you wearing your running shoes? B: I ___ go for a run.
pick.why: B decided before (the shoes are already on), so use going to.

pick.q: Watch out! You ___ hit that car!
pick.why: You can see it about to happen, so use are going to + base verb.

pick.q: We ___ going to stay in a hotel. It's too expensive.
pick.why: The negative uses be + not: We aren't going to stay.

pick.q: A: Oh no, I spilled my coffee! B: Don't worry. I ___ get a cloth.
pick.why: B decides at that moment, so here we use will, not going to: I'll get a cloth.

type.q: Look at the sky! It ___ (snow) soon.
type.why: Evidence now (the sky), so use going to: It's going to snow.

type.q: It's my New Year's resolution. I ___ (stop) eating junk food.
type.why: A resolution is an intention decided before, so use going to: I'm going to stop.

type.q: He's bought some paint because he ___ (paint) the bedroom.
type.why: The plan came first (he bought paint), so use going to: he's going to paint.

type.q: We've decided to wait. We ___ (not / buy) a house this year.
type.why: A decision made before speaking, negative: We aren't going to buy.

type.q: You talked about it all week. ___ (you / apply) for that manager job?
type.why: Asking about someone's plan: Are you going to apply?
You can see it about to happen, so use going to: It's going to fall.

type.q: I feel terrible. I think I ___ (be) sick.
type.why: Evidence from how you feel now: I'm going to be sick.

type.q: My son ___ (study) engineering after high school. He decided last year.
type.why: He decided last year, so this is a plan: He's going to study engineering.

spot.q: I going to call the bank this afternoon.
spot.why: Don't forget be: I'm (I am) going to call the bank.

spot.q: They are going to sells their old car.
spot.why: After going to, use the base verb with no -s: going to sell.

spot.q: Look at that man on the ladder! He will fall!
spot.why: We can see the danger now, so use going to: He's going to fall!

spot.q: Do you going to watch the game tonight?
spot.why: Going to questions use be, not do: Are you going to watch?

spot.q: I bought flour and eggs because I will bake a cake.
spot.why: The plan came before (you bought the flour), so use going to: I'm going to bake a cake.

order.a: I am going to look for a new job.
order.why: Subject + am going to + base verb: I am going to look for a new job.

order.a: Are you going to watch the hockey game?
order.why: Questions: Are + subject + going to + base verb.

order.a: It is going to be a cold winter.
order.why: A prediction: It is going to be + adjective + noun.

order.a: We are not going to eat out tonight.
alt: Tonight we are not going to eat out.
order.why: Negative: are + not + going to + base verb. We are not going to eat out.

pick.q: The traffic is terrible. We ___ be late for the meeting.
pick.why: We can see it now (the traffic), so use going to. 'Will to' is never correct.

pick.q: A: Why did you buy a guitar? B: I ___ learn to play it.
pick.why: B bought the guitar because of a plan made before, so use going to.

pick.q: My parents ___ going to retire next year.
pick.why: With they (my parents), use are: They are going to retire.

pick.q: Is she going to ___ a party for her birthday?
pick.why: After going to, always the base verb: going to have.

pick.q: A: I don't understand this form. B: Give it to me. I ___ help you.
pick.why: B decides at that moment, so use will: I'll help you.

pick.q: The kids are exhausted. They ___ going to stay up late tonight.
pick.why: The negative of going to uses be + not: They aren't going to stay up.

type.q: Look at that car! It ___ (crash) into the wall!
type.why: You can see it about to happen: It's going to crash.
I've decided shows a plan made before: I'm going to sell it.

type.q: She has decided. She ___ (not / take) the job. The pay is too low.
type.why: A decision made before speaking, negative: She isn't going to take the job.

type.q: You've moved all that old furniture into the garage. What ___ (you / do) with it?
type.why: Asking about a plan: What are you going to do with it?

type.q: He's far ahead of the other runners. He ___ (win) the race.
type.why: Evidence now (he's far ahead): He's going to win.

type.q: We ___ (paint) the kitchen yellow. We chose the colour last week.
type.why: The plan was made last week, so use going to: We're going to paint.
You can see it coming (you're late): We're going to miss the bus.

type.q: My brother ___ (become) a nurse. He has always wanted to help people.
type.why: A life plan or intention: He's going to become a nurse.

spot.q: We is going to have a barbecue on Sunday.
spot.why: With we, use are: We are going to have a barbecue.

spot.q: He's going to buying a new phone.
spot.why: After going to, use the base verb, not -ing: going to buy.

spot.q: Be careful! You will drop those eggs!
spot.why: You can see it about to happen, so use going to: You're going to drop them!

spot.q: What you are going to do this weekend?
spot.why: In questions, be comes before the subject: What are you going to do?

order.a: She is going to call you back later.
order.why: Subject + is going to + base verb: She is going to call you back later.

order.a: What are you going to do next summer?
order.why: Question word + are + you + going to + base verb.

order.a: I think it is going to rain.
order.why: A prediction: I think it is going to rain.

bank.q: The ice is very thin. Someone ___ fall through it.
bank.why: Evidence now (thin ice), so use going to. 'Will to' is never correct.

bank.q: A: Is that a new tent? B: Yes, we ___ go camping in August.
bank.why: They bought the tent for a plan made before, so use going to.

bank.q: A: There's someone at the door. B: Stay there. I ___ open it.
bank.why: B decides at that moment, so use will: I'll open it.

bank.q: I ___ going to eat that. It smells bad.
bank.why: The negative uses be + not: I am not going to eat that.

bank.q: When ___ they going to finish the new subway line?
bank.why: Going to questions use be: When are they going to finish?

bank.q: He's going to ___ his grandmother on Sunday.
bank.why: After going to, use the base verb: going to visit.

bank.q: My phone battery is at one percent. It ___ die any second.
bank.why: You can see it coming (1% battery): It's going to die.

bank.q: We've decided. We ___ rent an apartment downtown.
bank.why: We've decided shows a plan made before speaking, so use going to.

bank.q: Look at that dog! It ___ (jump) into the lake.
bank.why: You can see it about to happen: It's going to jump.

bank.q: I've made up my mind. I ___ (not / call) him again.
bank.why: A decision made before, negative: I'm not going to call him.

bank.q: She was thinking about the job in Calgary last week. ___ (she / take) it?
bank.why: Asking about someone's plan: Is she going to take it?

bank.q: They ___ (open) a bakery one day. It's their dream.
bank.why: A dream or intention: They're going to open a bakery one day.

bank.q: The other team is winning 5 to 0 with two minutes left. Our team ___ (lose).
bank.why: The score is the evidence: Our team is going to lose.

bank.q: I'm going to cleaning the garage this weekend.
bank.why: After going to, use the base verb: going to clean.

bank.q: Look at the time! We're going to be late.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. The time on the clock is the evidence, so going to is right.

bank.q: She going to start yoga classes in January.
bank.why: Don't forget be: She's (she is) going to start.

bank.q: A: The printer's not working. B: I'll take a look at it.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. B decides at that moment, so will is right.

bank.a: They are going to get married next spring.
alt: Next spring they are going to get married.
bank.why: Subject + are going to + base verb + time: They are going to get married next spring.

bank.a: Is it going to rain this afternoon?
bank.why: Question: Is + it + going to + base verb?

bank.a: I am not going to buy that dress.
bank.why: Negative: am + not + going to + base verb.
